stem:
The diagram shows $\triangle ABC$ with a right angle at $B$, $AB=5$, and $BC=12$. Vihaan wants the length of $AC$.

Which claim correctly applies $a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$?

options.text: $AC$ is the hypotenuse opposite the right angle, so $5^{2}+12^{2}=AC^{2}$ and $AC=13$.
Apply $5^{2}+12^{2}=AC^{2}$ even when the right-angle mark at $B$ is removed.
The right angle at $B$ is produced only after $5^{2}+12^{2}=AC^{2}$ is written.
Treat $AC$ as a leg and set $AC^{2}+5^{2}=12^{2}$.

teacher.key_rationale: In right triangle ABC with right angle at B, AC is the hypotenuse, so 25+144=AC^2 and AC=13. Dropping the right angle, reversing the relation, or mis-identifying the hypotenuse are wrong.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right-triangle figure to ABC right-angled at B with legs 5 and 12 for the hypotenuse hinge.
